title: First four consonants: ক ম ন ল
body:
# Lesson 1: First four consonants: ক ম ন ল

Every Bengali consonant carries a built-in vowel, **o**. So ক on its own is read **ko**. At the end of a word that o is usually dropped: কম is **kom**, not komo.

| Script | Sound | Note |
|---|---|---|
| ক | ko (k) | Plain k with no puff of air. Note the top bar (matra) that joins letters in a word. |
| ম | mo (m) | Small loop at the lower left; স (later) looks similar but has a hooked top. |
| ন | no (n) | A second n letter, ণ, comes later and sounds the same; ন is the common one. |
| ল | lo (l) | Round body with a small loop on the left; the loop sits low. |

## How they combine

Write letters left to right with no vowel marks and you get consonant + o, consonant + o... with the last o silent. ক + ল + ম = কলম **kolom**.

## Read these

Cover the right side, read the script aloud, then check.

- কম → kom: less, little
- মন → mon: mind, heart
- কলম → kolom: pen
- কমল → komol: lotus (also the name Komol)

cards.Notes: Plain k with no puff of air. Note the top bar (matra) that joins letters in a word.
Small loop at the lower left; স (later) looks similar but has a hooked top.
A second n letter, ণ, comes later and sounds the same; ন is the common one.
Round body with a small loop on the left; the loop sits low.
ক k + ম m: inherent o after k, final o silent.
ম m + ন n: inherent o after m, final o silent.
ক k + ল l + ম m: o after k and l, final o silent.
ক k + ম m + ল l: same pattern as কলম, k-o-m-o-l.
